description: Church of England parish church built in 1826-27 by John Davies. It is one of the early Commissioners' churches built after the Battle of Waterloo. It forms part of the Winchmore Hill Conservation Area. The chancel was added in 1888-89, and further extended for the church's centenary in 1928. The church is open daily, and there will be guided tours and a special exhibition 19-20 September.

factsheet.heading: History
paragraphs: St Paul's Church was built in 1826-27 to designs by by John Davies. It is one of the early Commissioners' churches built after the Battle of Waterloo, and the earliest in the borough of Enfield. It forms part of the Winchmore Hill Conservation Area. The chancel was added in 1888-89, and further extended for the church's centenrary in 1928.

factsheet.heading: Historic and contemporary uses
paragraphs: St Paul's has been a place of Christian worship for almost 200 years. Today it continues to be a thriving, intergenerational church. The building is open every day of every week for people to visit, look round, pray and reflect.

factsheet.heading: Exhibition and tours
paragraphs: The church will be open every day. Additionally, on Saturday 19 September (9am-5pm) and Sunday 20 September (12pm-5pm) there will be an exhibition of the church's archives, and guided tours of the building at 2pm, given by members of the clergy.

factsheet.heading: Essential information
paragraphs: Although the church will be open between 9am and 5pm, please note that small services take place on most weekdays 9am-9.45am, and on Wednesdays 12.30pm-1pm. Visitors are welcome to look round the church during these times, but are asked to be mindful of services taking place.
Sunday services take place at 8am, 9.15am and 10.30am. Visitors are very welcome to attend these services, but it will not be possible to look round the building during these times.
Opening times are subject to change (e.g. if a funeral is taking place).
